entries.clue: Some prang started causing anxiety (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: 'Some' asks for only part of what follows, so the answer is a piece cut from the next words.

blocks.note: The letters run across the gap, starting after the P-R of prang and ending before the rest of started.

annotation.surface: A minor car bump leaves the driver rattled.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'prang' is British slang for a small car crash, which is what makes the surface sound natural; the letters straddle the gap between its two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Angst is the German loanword for a deep, nagging anxiety, and English uses it as a straight synonym.

entries.clue: Ron in no trouble as it's easily laundered (3-4)

indicatorNotes.trouble: Letters 'in trouble' are in disorder, so they get rearranged.

blocks.note: The eight letters of RON IN NO, rearranged.

annotation.surface: Ron has no worries about the washing because it comes out of the machine without fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: The little word 'in' looks like it places Ron somewhere, but it is part of the letters to shuffle, and 'no' reads as a word rather than fodder too.
annotation.definitionFit: Non-iron fabric dries smooth and needs no pressing, which is exactly what makes it easy to launder.

entries.clue: Odd spider near Tuscan city (5)

indicatorNotes.Odd: 'Odd' points at the odd-numbered positions, so take the first, third, fifth letters and so on.

blocks.note: The first, third and fifth letters of spider.
The first and third letters of near, carrying the count on.

annotation.surface: A strange spider is lurking close to an Italian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd' reads as 'strange' in the surface, describing the spider, and the letter run carries on into 'near' rather than stopping at the end of the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: Siena is the walled hill city in Tuscany, famous for its Palio horse race.

entries.clue: Woman finds happiness at church (5)

blocks.note: Joy is happiness.
CE is the Church of England.

annotation.surface: A woman discovers contentment through her faith.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Woman' is a crossword signal for a girl's name, and CE for 'church' is one of the most common abbreviations in the genre.
annotation.definitionFit: Joyce is a woman's first name, and a name like this is defined by the broad class it belongs to.

entries.clue: A politician's after gold for public speaking (7)

indicatorNotes.after: 'After' says the politician comes later than the gold, so the gold is written first.

blocks.note: OR is gold in heraldry, from the French.
The article, kept as it is.
A Tory is a British Conservative politician; the 's is 'is', joining the pieces.

annotation.surface: A politician chasing gold medals in debating.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', not a possessive, and it reads 'a politician is after gold'. OR for gold comes from heraldry.
annotation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, especially the formal, eloquent kind.

entries.clue: Grass on Catholic leader for beliefs (5)

indicatorNotes.on: 'On' means added on to, so the grass is attached after the other piece.
indicatorNotes.leader: A leader stands at the front, so the leader of a word is its first letter.

blocks.note: The first letter of Catholic.
A reed is a tall grass of wet ground.

annotation.surface: Someone informs on the head of the Catholic church because of his faith.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass on' is British slang for informing on someone, and the surface leans on it; here 'grass' is simply a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of religious beliefs, from the Latin 'credo', I believe.

entries.clue: Coming in first if frozen rigid (5)

indicatorNotes.Coming in: Something 'coming in' is inside, so the answer sits within the words that follow.

blocks.note: The run begins with the last two letters of first, takes all of if, and ends on the opening letter of frozen.

annotation.surface: Someone arriving first is frozen stiff with cold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First' tempts you to count positions or write 1ST, but it only lends its last two letters to the hidden run.
annotation.definitionFit: Stiff and rigid are plain synonyms: both describe something that will not bend.

entries.clue: Like little photo of jelly (5)

blocks.note: 'Like' and 'as' both mean in the manner of.
A pic is a short word for a picture or photo.

annotation.surface: A small snapshot of a wobbly dessert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a shortened word here, PIC being the clipped form of picture.
annotation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat or fish stock, used to set cold dishes.

entries.clue: Hope Ravel piece is musical drama (5)

indicatorNotes.piece: A piece is a part of a whole, so the answer is a part of the words before it.

blocks.note: The run starts after the H of Hope and stops two letters into Ravel.

annotation.surface: A work by the composer Ravel described as a stage piece with music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' pretends to be a musical composition by Ravel, which suits the surface perfectly; it is the instruction to take a piece of 'Hope Ravel'.
annotation.definitionFit: An opera is a drama set to music and sung throughout.

entries.clue: Weight of cask, say (5)

indicatorNotes.say: 'Say' means spoken aloud, so the answer is a word that sounds like the one before it.

blocks.note: A tun is a large cask for wine or beer; said aloud it gives a metric weight.

annotation.surface: Asking how heavy a barrel is.
annotation.walkthrough: TUN is an old word for a big barrel, worth keeping because setters use it often.
annotation.definitionFit: A tonne is the metric unit of weight equal to a thousand kilograms.

entries.clue: Push pea around and become fit (5,2)

indicatorNotes.around: Letters moved around are shifted into a new order.

blocks.note: The seven letters of PUSH PEA, rearranged.

annotation.surface: A fussy eater nudges a pea about the plate and hopes to get healthy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Push' looks like an instruction to move the pea, but it is fodder alongside it; 'around' works on both words together.
annotation.definitionFit: To shape up is to get into good physical condition, which is what becoming fit means.

entries.clue: Prestigious car, rarer model in Formula One (7)

indicatorNotes.model: To model something is to shape it, so the letters get reshaped.
indicatorNotes.in: 'In' places one thing inside another, so the reshaped letters go between the others.

blocks.note: The first letter of Formula, as on the F1 badge.
RARER, rearranged.
One is I in Roman numerals, the other half of F1.

annotation.surface: A luxury car described as a very rare model in motor racing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' passes for a car model in the surface; it is the rearranging instruction. Formula One shortens to F1, and the 1 becomes I.
annotation.definitionFit: Ferrari is the Italian maker of expensive sports cars, the byword for a prestige car.

entries.clue: More rum and Pernod derived inside (5)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'Inside' says the answer is within the words just named.

blocks.note: The run takes the last two letters of Pernod and the first three of derived.

annotation.surface: More spirits and aniseed liqueur taken in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rum' wants to be the drink, keeping company with Pernod; it is the old adjective meaning strange.
annotation.definitionFit: Rum is a British informal adjective for strange or peculiar, so more rum means odder.

entries.clue: Agreement with penultimate element (5)

blocks.note: An element is a unit, one of the parts that make up a whole.
Y is the penultimate letter of the alphabet, just before Z.

annotation.surface: A deal involving the second-to-last chemical element.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penultimate' seems to describe the element, but on its own it points to the alphabet's next-to-last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Unity is a state of agreement or harmony between people.

entries.clue: Lurching tourist (7)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Lurching' is a participle, not a noun; the setter lets it stand for one who lurches, a person who trips.

blocks.note: Someone lurching is stumbling along, one who trips over their feet.
A British word for a day-tourist, someone out on a short excursion.

annotation.surface: A sightseer staggering about unsteadily.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses of 'trip' do the work: a stumble and an outing.
annotation.definitionFit: A tripper is a British word for a tourist on a short outing, and the word also describes someone who trips and lurches.

entries.clue: Tokyo rebuilt another Japanese city (5)

indicatorNotes.rebuilt: Something rebuilt is put together again differently, so the letters are reassembled.

blocks.note: The five letters of TOKYO, rearranged.

annotation.surface: Tokyo is reconstructed as a second Japanese city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' is part of the definition: the answer is a Japanese city other than the one named.
annotation.definitionFit: Kyoto is Japan's former imperial capital, a city distinct from Tokyo.

entries.clue: Less bland Moroccan town (7)

blocks.note: The comparative of tangy: sharper and zestier, so less bland.
The port city on Morocco's side of the Strait of Gibraltar.

annotation.surface: A Moroccan town with more flavour than the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words are spelt the same but said differently: the town stresses the second syllable, the comparative the first.
annotation.definitionFit: Tangier means more tangy, the opposite of blander, and is also Morocco's northern port city.

entries.clue: Woman coming round all right to call up (5)

indicatorNotes.coming round: Coming round something means encircling it, so the woman surrounds the other piece.

blocks.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
OK means all right.

annotation.surface: A woman visits to phone someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coming round' sounds like a friendly visit; it means the woman's name wraps around OK.
annotation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up a memory or feeling, bringing it to mind.

entries.clue: Restrict most untidy houses (5)

indicatorNotes.houses: What a phrase houses is held inside it, so the answer is lodged within those words.

blocks.note: The run takes the last two letters of most and the first three of untidy.

annotation.surface: Limiting the messiest homes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Houses' reads as a noun in the surface, messy homes, but it is a verb meaning contains.
annotation.definitionFit: To stunt is to restrict growth or development, as poor soil stunts a plant.

entries.clue: Agree with incredible youth leader (5)

indicatorNotes.leader: A leader goes first, so the leader of a word is its opening letter.

blocks.note: A tall story is an incredible one.
The first letter of youth.

annotation.surface: Going along with an amazing leader of young people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tall' for 'incredible' comes from the phrase 'tall tale', not from height.
annotation.definitionFit: Figures that tally agree with each other, as matching records do.

entries.clue: Drive out to get composer (5)

indicatorNotes.out: 'Out' can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are put out of their usual order.

blocks.note: The five letters of DRIVE, rearranged.

annotation.surface: Heading out in the car to pick up a musician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drive out' reads as one phrasal verb, a trip in the car; split it and the second word works on the first.
annotation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian composer of Aida and La Traviata.

entries.clue: Weren't for the most part moved to begin again (5)

indicatorNotes.for the most part: 'For the most part' means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter.
indicatorNotes.moved: Letters moved are shifted into a new order.

blocks.note: WERENT without its final T.

annotation.surface: People were not, on the whole, inspired to start over.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'weren't' is ignored, leaving WERENT, and trimming it before rearranging is the order of work.
annotation.definitionFit: To renew something is to begin it again, as with a subscription or an effort.

entries.clue: Somehow I attain role of queen (7)

indicatorNotes.Somehow: 'Somehow' means in some way or other, so the letters are arranged in some other way.

blocks.note: The seven letters of I ATTAIN, rearranged.

annotation.surface: An actor wonders how they landed the part of a queen.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an actor's surprise at being cast; the part in question is in Shakespeare.
annotation.definitionFit: Titania is the queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, a stage role.

entries.clue: Model pleads for jobs (5)

blocks.note: The Model T was Henry Ford's famous early car.
To plead is to ask earnestly.

annotation.surface: A fashion model begs to be hired.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' paints a catwalk model in the surface; crosswords use it for the letter T through the Ford Model T.
annotation.definitionFit: Tasks and jobs are plain synonyms: pieces of work to be done.

entries.clue: Family doctor at home of key person in organisation (7)

blocks.note: Your kin are your family.
A GP is a general practitioner, the British family doctor.
Someone at home is in.

annotation.surface: The family doctor making a house call to someone important in a firm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as one phrase, the British term for a GP, but 'family' is KIN on its own and 'doctor' alone gives GP.
annotation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the most important person in a group, originally the central pin in bowling.

entries.clue: Pile out after spiv's initial patter (5)

indicatorNotes.out: 'Out' can mean disordered, so the letters are knocked out of their order.
indicatorNotes.after: 'After' puts this piece later than the one named next, so it follows it.
indicatorNotes.initial: An initial is the first letter of a name, so only the opening letter is taken.

blocks.note: The first letter of spiv.
PILE, rearranged.

annotation.surface: A dodgy dealer's sales pitch pours out in a heap.
annotation.walkthrough: A spiv is a flashy British petty crook of the post-war black market, just the sort to have a spiel, which makes the surface hang together.
annotation.definitionFit: A spiel is a glib, practised line of talk, the same as a salesman's patter.

entries.clue: Second moderately hot group (5)

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second.
Warm is moderately hot.

annotation.surface: The runner-up in a band that is only lukewarm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like it describes the group; it is the unit of time, abbreviated S.
annotation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large moving group, of bees or of people.

entries.clue: Unfair lending causes American rage, but not loud (5)

indicatorNotes.but not: 'But not' excludes something, so the named letter is taken away.

blocks.note: US for American.
Fury is rage.
F is forte, loud in music; it is removed from FURY.

annotation.surface: Loan sharks make Americans quietly furious.
annotation.walkthrough: F for loud comes from the musical marking forte, the opposite of P for piano, soft.
annotation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at an unreasonably high rate of interest.
